fields.group: g1 = L01-L17, g2 = L18-L33, g3 = L34-L49; each group had its own two readers and adjudicator
fields.A: settled answer to (A): would a regulatory reader record this as one of the letter's questions
fields.B: settled answer to (B): does one contiguous span hold exactly the agency's words of this question
fields.B_inside: when B is no: what is inside, by line
fields.readerA / readerB: each reader's own (A) and (B); the full reader files are in raw/
fields.settled_by: agreed = both readers gave the same (A) and (B) and the adjudicator confirmed it on reading; adjudicated = the readers differed and the adjudicator settled it (see disagreements.json)

g1.method: Every letter L01-L17 was read in full (lines JSON.stringify-ed, sha256 and UTF-16 length checked against questions.json). Every one of the 63 slices was read as letter.slice(start, end) with 25 characters either side, first/last words confirmed, and scanned for control and non-ASCII characters (only U+000C in Q2 and Q44; U+000B at L06 offset 22 is outside every slice). Line breaks, including empty docx paragraphs, are not counted as foreign content, as both readers did. All 63 agreed questions were spot-checked (well above 5 per group); no spot-check found both readers wrong. No letter has an unlisted question.

g2.method: Every one of the 44 spans was sliced in Node by UTF-16 [start,end), printed with JSON.stringify beside the numbered lines of its letter, and scanned for any code unit other than LF outside printable ASCII and CJK text; every letter was read whole for (C). All 43 agreed questions were therefore spot-checked (well above 5); none showed both readers wrong. The one disagreement (76) is settled below. Neither reader listed a missing question and the adjudicator found none.
g2.missingChecked: Read every letter L18-L33 whole. Non-questions confirmed: L18 line 26 response instruction and line 28 closer; L24 line 5 closer; L25 line 5 lead-in; L28 items 1-3 are parts of Question 1; L30 line 13 以上 end marker. No question a reader would record is absent from the list.

g3.method: Every letter L34-L49 was read in full (lines JSON.stringify-ed; sha256 and UTF-16 length of every letter checked against questions.json; questions.json sha256 checked). Every one of the 70 slices (n108-n177) was read as letter.slice(start, end) with 60 characters either side, first and last words confirmed, and scanned for control and non-ASCII characters: none exist anywhere in L34-L49. Line breaks, including empty docx paragraphs, are not counted as foreign content, as both readers did and as g1 settled. The readers agree on (A) and (B) for all 70 questions; all 70 were spot-checked and no spot-check found both readers wrong. For the 12 meeting questions (L45, L47, L49) both readers' (B) 'no' was tested against the literal README wording: the span is the sponsor's text, which does not belong; read as question plus response it would take in the sponsor's text and the response label; only the agency's response alone is a clean span, and that is a different text, recorded under missing. Every (C) item either reader listed was read at its line and settled; the settled missing items carry their exact [start, end) UTF-16 span, each checked clean. A (C) disagreement is counted when the readers place an item at a different line or a different first word; 'C-location' means they chose different text for the same obligation.
